name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
summary: A static mobility exercise performed in a half-kneeling position to stretch the iliopsoas and rectus femoris of the rear leg.

setup: Assume a half-kneeling position with one knee resting on the floor directly beneath your hip and the other foot planted flat out front, forming 90-degree angles at both knees.
Maintain an upright posture with your hands resting on your hips or front thigh.
steps: Engage your abdominals and actively squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg to tilt your pelvis slightly backward into a neutral or posterior position.
Gently shift your weight forward into your front foot just until you feel a firm stretch along the front of the trailing hip and thigh.
Breathe steadily and hold this position without allowing your lower back to arch.
Carefully ease out of the stretch, reposition, and repeat on the opposite leg.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply throughout the hold, using each exhalation to relax deeper into the stretch without losing pelvic alignment.
cues: Shift the hips, do not arch the back

common_faults.fault: Arching the lumbar spine to create an illusion of forward movement.
common_faults.correction: Keep your ribcage down and brace your core so the movement comes exclusively from hip extension rather than lower-back extension.

common_faults.fault: Lurching too far forward and losing pelvic control.
common_faults.correction: Only glide forward an inch or two; initiating the stretch with glute activation and a posterior pelvic tilt produces tension with minimal forward travel.

precautions: Use a padded exercise mat or cushion beneath the kneeling knee if you experience discomfort on hard flooring.
